Over ~9 years a deliberate but US-limited Russia-vs-Baltic clash is plausible yet remains the tail case.

Conditional on any offensive detonation occurring at all, the most salient first-use scenarios (Russian tactical use in Ukraine, an India-Pakistan exchange spilling onto non-nuclear neighbors, Israel-Iran) frequently put the impact on or near a non-nuclear state. Ukraine is the leading candidate, so a non-nuclear-state fatality is the likely (not certain) form.

Of the three buckets (deliberate, inadvertent, accidental), inadvertent launch from a mistaken counterattack belief is historically the rarest actual cause; deliberate use dominates first-detonation scenarios. Conditional on a first detonation, inadvertent is a low-probability mechanism.

Accidental/unauthorized detonation (safeguard failure, rogue actor) is a low-probability mechanism relative to a deliberate decision to use; modern PALs and procedures make accidental detonation the least likely first event. Deliberate remains the dominant residual.

Conditional on >100 offensive detonations (a major nuclear war), a >=10% one-year drop in global goods trade is near-certain: even the 2009 financial crisis cut world merchandise trade ~20%+, and a large nuclear exchange would devastate ports, infrastructure, and economies far more.

China-India relations are in a 2025-26 normalization/thaw with managed friction; both are nuclear and economically interdependent. Even the deadliest recent clash (Galwan 2020) killed ~24, far below the 1000/yr threshold, so a war-scale conflict by 2035 is a low-probability tail despite unresolved border disputes.

Conditional on at least one HEMP attack by 2030, the count is heavily right-skewed at 1: a HEMP attack would be an extraordinary escalation, almost certainly isolated, with multiple attacks implying an ongoing nuclear exchange. Median 1, with a thin tail to a handful.

Most plausible state detonation scenarios (single tactical/demonstration use, battlefield or military/silo targets) are not dense-city strikes, pulling the fraction low; but a full countervalue exchange would push much of the mass onto cities. Wide distribution centered around 0.2, spanning 0 to near 1.
